title.value: Trade-off between accuracy and fairness of data-driven building and indoor environment models: A comparative study of pre-processing methods
title.justification: The title clearly reflects the content of the paper, focusing on the balance between accuracy and fairness in data-driven models related to buildings and indoor environments.
title.quote: Trade-off between accuracy and fairness of data-driven building and indoor environment models: A comparative study of pre-processing methods

extractions.description: This paper explores the balance between accuracy and fairness in data-driven models for building and indoor environments. It introduces three types of fairness in building engineering, examines two types of fairness, and proposes pre-processing methods to improve fairness in predictive models used for lighting status prediction. The study compares these methods in terms of their impact on accuracy and fairness across various scenarios.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central focus of the paper is on improving the predictive accuracy and fairness of data-driven models used in energy management and indoor environments, which directly ties to sustainability by enhancing energy efficiency in buildings.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This paper addresses a new research problem called fairness-aware prediction of data-driven building and indoor environment models.

primary_category.justification: The study focuses on data-driven models for buildings, specifically looking at energy management and efficiency, which aligns with climate change mitigation efforts through improved energy efficiency in buildings.
primary_category.quote: These models could be further integrated into a model predictive controller (MPC) that can predefine optimal control signals based on users’ demand, and control relevant devices via HEMS to achieve cost/energy saving, or peak shifting.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no explicit secondary sustainable development areas addressed in the paper apart from energy efficiency in buildings.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper's focus is on building and indoor environment models which are used to predict variables that can influence energy management in buildings, directly correlating with energy efficiency improvements.
primary_sub_category.quote: As smart home energy management systems (HEMS) and sensors are rapidly gaining popularity, an abundance of information could be dynamically collected from buildings [1]. This has increased attention to developing data-driven prediction models for: indoor air temperature, building energy consumption, occupants' thermal comfort.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no explicit secondary sub-categories relevant to the content of the paper beyond energy efficiency in buildings.

applications.justification: The paper involves case studies that use the proposed methods for predicting lighting status, which is a specific application within the scope of building energy efficiency.
applications.quote: The proposed methods are compared to two existing pre-processing methods in a case study for lighting status prediction in an apartment building.

new_primary_category.justification: The current classification categories adequately describe the paper's focus and areas of interest.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The existing sub-categories fit the paper's focus on building energy efficiency, so no new sub-category is needed.
